patch.value: GH-1138: linked test name filters can pass after executing zero tests

Track GitHub issue #1138: linked test commands using runner name filters can exit zero after matching no tests. `pm test <id> --run` records a green receipt even though the evidence command performed no assertions, silently invalidating the durable verification claim after a test rename or typo.

Add an SDK-owned executed-test assertion primitive and declarative minimum-count field; recognize supported runner receipts without brittle prose-only heuristics; fail zero-test filtered commands closed; preserve explicit non-test smoke commands; add unit, integration, CLI, MCP/schema, history, Node runner, and temp-workspace acceptance coverage.
pm 2026.8.28, Node 26.5.0, Linux; node --test command with --test-name-pattern matching zero tests
Link a `node --test --test-name-pattern` command whose pattern matches no test, run it through `pm test <id> --run`, and observe ok true with the runner reporting pass 0.
A linked test declares and enforces a minimum executed-test count through a public SDK-owned runner receipt contract; zero-test filtered runs fail closed with actionable evidence.
The child process exits zero, pm reports the linked test passed, and no structured field distinguishes zero executed tests from a real passing assertion.
Renamed or mistyped test filters silently turn immutable PM verification evidence into a tautology, misleading later agents and release gates.
